unit.name: Machine learning work feels like debugging
unit.description: The lecture generalizes from the speech example to a process lesson: ML progress depends on disciplined debugging loops whose shape is constrained by training time, and that speed turns directly into product competitiveness.
unit.summary: The instructor argues that ML work feels more like debugging than classical software construction because you do not know in advance which data, bias-variance, or mismatch issue will surface next [ts=2892s] [ts=2963s]. He describes a daily rhythm of launching training runs, inspecting results the next morning, performing error analysis, coding a fix, and relaunching overnight so the team removes roughly one blocker per day [ts=3006s] [ts=3070s]. The exact operating cadence depends on whether training takes minutes, hours, or weeks, but the meta-principle is unchanged: shorten the loop between evidence and the next experiment [ts=3156s] [ts=3302s]. He closes by showing that a team that is merely 2x slower in iteration can be dramatically less competitive because performance compounds over calendar time [ts=3358s] [ts=3423s].

key_points.text: Machine learning development is best treated as iterative debugging rather than one-shot implementation.
A healthy team cadence is train, inspect, analyze, fix, and relaunch on a regular schedule.
Training-job duration should shape how the team plans experiments and analysis work.
Iteration speed compounds into market advantage because faster teams reach stronger models earlier.

kp_catalog.name: Debugging cadence should match training-time constraints
kp_catalog.description: An operational principle for structuring evaluation and engineering work around the runtime of experiments.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Debugging cadence is important process guidance, but supports the broader diagnostic loop.

kp_catalog.name: Iteration speed as a core AI project lever
kp_catalog.description: The idea that faster experiment-selection and execution loops matter more than small local modeling choices because they compound over time.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Iteration speed frames the project-strategy mindset but is not a technical prerequisite gate.
